passage: I've known Hrithik since first year, so I noticed it on Saturday at the canteen. His partner Neel came over and Hrithik went quiet. He pulled his shoulders in a little and moved his chair back a few inches when Neel leaned close. When Neel's phone buzzed, Hrithik glanced at it, then away, and gave a smile that stopped before his eyes. Maybe he was just tired. Maybe it was nothing to do with Neel. I couldn't tell. Afterwards I texted him, "Want to grab tea, just us? No pressure." He said yes, and I said I'd listen and that I'd help find someone to talk to if he wanted. I'm Tejas, and I don't want to guess for him.

qa.q: Where did Tejas see Hrithik go quiet?
qa.a: Tejas saw it in the canteen.

qa.q: What might Hrithik have been feeling when moving the chair back?
qa.a: Hrithik may have been uncomfortable around Neel, as the pulled-in shoulders and the smile that stopped before the eyes suggest. But Tejas admits it could be tiredness, so the cues are not proof.

qa.q: What did Tejas do that respected Hrithik's choice?
qa.a: Tejas texted a private, low-pressure invitation for tea, and offered to listen and help find support without pushing.

qa.q: How might Tejas feel about not being able to read Hrithik's cues?
qa.a: Tejas seems concerned but careful, unsure whether it was tiredness or something about Neel, so Tejas offers tea and listening rather than guessing for Hrithik.

passage:
Monday. Pooja noticed that Vasudha flinched when their manager Mr. Bhatia called her name across the open office. It was small: a quick shrug of the shoulders, eyes down. Pooja thought it might be the manager's tone.

Wednesday. During the stand-up meeting Vasudha stood at the back with her arms wrapped across her chest and backed off when Mr. Bhatia walked by. Pooja stopped assuming and decided to ask privately.

Friday. At lunch Pooja said, "You seemed tense around Mr. Bhatia. I'm here if you want to talk." Vasudha was quiet, then said thanks and that she'd think about it. Pooja told her about the company's employee support line and left it with her.

qa.q: What did Pooja tell Vasudha about at lunch?
qa.a: Pooja told Vasudha about the company's employee support line.

qa.q: What did Vasudha's arms across the chest suggest?
qa.a: It suggested Vasudha felt uneasy or wanted to protect herself around the manager, though the cue is only a hint and could have other causes.

qa.q: What could Pooja do if Vasudha does not want to talk yet?
qa.a: Respect that, keep the door open, and be steady and non-pushy, letting Vasudha decide when to use the support line.

qa.q: What might Vasudha be thinking after Pooja offers help?
qa.a: Vasudha may feel relieved that someone noticed, yet unsure about speaking up, which fits the quiet reply and the wish to think about it.

passage: Listen, Wasim, you asked why I always ask new trainees how they're doing, so I'll tell you. I'm Pranav uncle to you all now, but at twenty I worked the night shift at a print press with my friend Gopal. Our supervisor had a loud voice and a heavy hand on the desk. I noticed Gopal would flinch every time the man came near, step back half a pace, cross his arms tight over his chest. At first I told myself Gopal was just tired. Then one night I saw him wince when the supervisor clapped his shoulder. I didn't say anything in front of anyone. At the tea break, outside, I just asked, "Gopal, is everything okay with him?" Gopal said nothing for a long time. Then he talked. I listened, and I told him about the workers' welfare officer. He went the next week. It was his choice. I only walked with him to the door.

qa.q: Where did young Pranav and Gopal work?
qa.a: On the night shift at a print press.

qa.q: What might Gopal have been feeling when the supervisor came near?
qa.a: His flinching, stepping back and crossed arms suggest he felt afraid or uncomfortable around the supervisor; tiredness was another possible reading, which is why Pranav asked instead of assuming.

qa.q: What turning point in the story let Gopal get help?
qa.a: Pranav chose to ask privately at the tea break, listened, and told Gopal about the welfare officer, leaving the decision to him.

qa.q: What would change if Pranav had asked Gopal in front of the others?
qa.a: Gopal might have denied everything or felt exposed near the supervisor; the private tea-break moment made it safer for him to talk.

passage: Lunch at the call centre was exactly twenty minutes, and the queue for the microwave took ten. Seema had noticed it all week: whenever team leader Harsh walked past, Nitin went very still, pulled his chair in and hunched over his keyboard. Once, when Harsh leaned over his shoulder, Nitin jerked his head back as if expecting a blow. It could be nothing. Maybe Nitin just hated being watched. But Seema couldn't shake it. With eight minutes left, she found Nitin on the back stairs with his tiffin. "Can I sit?" He nodded. "I've seen you tense up when Harsh comes by. You don't have to tell me anything. I just wanted to ask if you're okay." Nitin stared at his rice. "He shouts at me when nobody's around." Seema listened, then said, "HR has a confidential complaints line. I can sit with you when you call, or not. Your call." The bell rang. Nitin said, "Stay after shift?" She stayed.

qa.q: How long was lunch at the call centre?
qa.a: Exactly twenty minutes.

qa.q: What might Nitin have been feeling when Harsh leaned over his shoulder?
qa.a: Jerking his head back suggests he felt afraid and on guard; Seema also considered that he might just hate being watched, so she did not treat it as proof.

qa.q: How did Seema support Nitin without pushing him?
qa.a: She asked privately, said he did not have to tell her anything, listened, and offered the confidential HR line with her company only if he wanted it.

qa.q: What would change if Seema had confronted Harsh herself in front of the team?
qa.a: Nitin might have felt exposed and lost control over what happened next; checking privately kept the choice with him.

passage: Chetan had known Amandeep since school, and she had always been the loudest laugh in the room. At the café in Chandigarh she was quieter. When her boyfriend Rishi reached across to fix her collar, she flinched and pulled her shoulders in. Later, when Rishi's voice sharpened about the bill, she pulled her sleeves down over her hands and looked at the door. Chetan told himself couples have bad days. Still, he texted her that night: "Coffee tomorrow, just us?" At the bench outside the library, he said, "You seemed tense yesterday. Tell me to back off if you want. I'm just checking." Amandeep was quiet, then said Rishi "gets angry sometimes". Chetan didn't argue or rush her. He said he was on her side and gave her the number of the women's helpline and the college counsellor's timings. "Whatever you choose, I'm here." She saved both numbers.

qa.q: Where did Chetan and Amandeep meet the next day?
qa.a: At the bench outside the library.

qa.q: What might Amandeep have been feeling at the café?
qa.a: Her flinching, pulled-in shoulders and glance at the door suggest she felt scared or uncomfortable near Rishi; Chetan knew it could also just be a bad day, so he checked instead of concluding.

qa.q: What did Chetan do that respected Amandeep's choice?
qa.a: He asked privately, let her set the pace, said he was on her side, and gave her the helpline and counsellor's timings without telling her what to do.

qa.q: What would change if Chetan had challenged Rishi at the café?
qa.a: It could have embarrassed Amandeep or made things riskier for her, and she might have stopped confiding; asking privately kept her in charge.

passage:
Devika waited until Rehana's shift at the café was over and they were walking to the bus stop.
"Can I ask something? You don't have to answer."
"Okay..."
"Every time your manager walked past the counter today, you flinched. You kept pulling your sleeves down, too. Are you alright?"
Rehana stopped walking. "He shouts a lot. Last week he grabbed my wrist when I got an order wrong."
"I'm really glad you told me. That's not okay, and it isn't your fault."
"I don't want a scene. I need this internship for my credits."
"It's your call. But Ms Pinto at the internship cell handles placements. Want me to sit with you while you ring her?"
Rehana took a long breath, then dialled on speaker.
"Rehana, thank you for telling me," Ms Pinto said. "You don't need to go back tomorrow. Come to my office at five today, both of you if you like, and we'll decide the next step together."
Rehana's shoulders dropped a little. "Five. We'll be there."

qa.q: What did the manager do last week?
qa.a: He grabbed Rehana's wrist when she got an order wrong.

qa.q: What was Rehana worried about when Devika asked?
qa.a: Rehana felt scared of the manager and anxious about causing a scene, because she needed the internship for her credits.

qa.q: How did Devika respect Rehana's choice while still helping?
qa.a: Devika asked privately, said Rehana didn't have to answer, listened, said it wasn't Rehana's fault, and offered to sit beside Rehana during the call, leaving the decision to Rehana.

qa.q: How did Ms Pinto treat Rehana's call?
qa.a: Ms Pinto took it seriously and acted the same day, thanking Rehana, saying she need not go back tomorrow, and meeting them at five.

grounding: It illustrates a young adult noticing a friend's flinching and covering up near a manager, checking privately, listening, and supporting the friend's own choice to get help.
